name: Integra Command System
description: Canonical, host-agnostic command catalog for Integra workflows and modifiers.

commands.description: Understand the request, inspect project context, select and sequence the smallest useful set of workflows, then present a reviewable plan.
whenToUse: Use for broad, cross-stage or end-to-end product work that may require several specialist workflows.
Use when the desired outcome is clear but discovery, design, implementation and QA still need sequencing.
notFor: Do not replace a clearly focused specialist workflow.
Do not treat orchestration as permission to edit source.
inputs: User goal, intended users and explicit constraints
Repository guidance and current product state when available

commands.description: Clarify user needs, task flows, constraints and information architecture before visual direction or implementation.
whenToUse: Use when the user task, journey, navigation or information architecture is not clear.
Use before visual direction when content and tasks need structuring.
notFor: Do not use for a fully specified component that only needs implementation.
Do not substitute it for a visual critique.
inputs: Product purpose and primary audience
Known user tasks, content groups and constraints

commands.description: Create a contextual visual thesis, experience archetype, design principles and token direction.
whenToUse: Use to define a visual thesis, product-specific design brief, archetype and token direction.
Use when the current interface lacks a coherent visual system.
notFor: Do not use when only one already-specified component needs implementation.
Do not use for a narrow technical research question.
inputs: Product context, audience and primary task
Existing brand assets, tokens and restrictions
Platform and accessibility requirements

commands.description: Research references, patterns or technical questions and separate verified evidence from interpretation.
whenToUse: Use when a design or technical decision needs evidence from references or official documentation.
Use to compare specific interfaces or inspect a concrete interaction pattern.
notFor: Do not research generic inspiration when local evidence already answers the question.
Do not reproduce a competitor's page, copy, assets or brand identity.
inputs: Narrow research question and target behavior
Permitted URLs, screenshots or named sources
Current product context and decision to support

commands.description: Generate a new UI component or screen from an approved brief and direction.
whenToUse: Use to implement one sufficiently specified UI component, screen or interaction.
Use when the brief and visual direction are clear enough to produce a reviewable implementation.
notFor: Do not use alone for an end-to-end product request with unresolved stages.
Do not use when substantial existing behavior must be preserved; choose refactor.
inputs: Approved brief or clear component purpose
Target framework, stack and local conventions
Content, interaction states and acceptance criteria

commands.description: Improve existing UI code while preserving behavior, semantics, project conventions and public APIs.
whenToUse: Use to improve existing UI code while preserving behavior, semantics and public interfaces.
Use for maintainability, component boundaries and targeted cleanup.
notFor: Do not use to create a new screen from scratch.
Do not treat critique as authorization to modify source.
inputs: Existing source files and relevant tests
Behavioral invariants, public APIs and call sites
Project conventions and approved scope

commands.description: Review a page or component for product clarity, hierarchy, usability and visual consistency.
whenToUse: Use for focused review of product clarity, content hierarchy, composition or visual consistency.
Use when the user wants findings before deciding whether to modify code.
notFor: Do not substitute for a full technical, accessibility or performance audit.
Do not classify subjective style preference as a defect without context.
inputs: Target page, component or screenshot
Primary user task and relevant product context

commands.description: Run a broad quality review covering responsive behavior, interaction states, accessibility signals and performance risks.
whenToUse: Use for a broad review of responsive behavior, interaction states, accessibility signals and performance risks.
Use when multiple quality dimensions should be assessed together.
notFor: Do not use when the only requested scope is accessibility.
Do not claim global WCAG or performance conformance from partial static checks.
inputs: Target source or running page
Relevant viewports and interaction states
Available automated checks and measured performance evidence

commands.description: Perform a focused accessibility review with evidence, impact and actionable remediation.
whenToUse: Use when semantics, keyboard operation, accessible names, focus or contrast are the primary concern.
Use for a focused accessibility audit and evidence-backed remediation plan.
notFor: Do not use for a broad visual critique with no accessibility question.
Do not claim page-wide WCAG conformance from incomplete evidence.
inputs: Target UI and relevant interaction states
Accessibility target and supported input modes
Actual foreground/background pairs when contrast is assessed

commands.description: Identify repeated patterns and define or refine tokens, components and usage guidance.
whenToUse: Use when repeated UI patterns should become shared components, tokens or usage rules.
Use to inventory an existing design system or define its component contracts.
notFor: Do not abstract a one-off element without evidence of reuse.
Do not replace an established system without a migration plan.
inputs: Existing components, tokens and documentation
Repeated UI examples and behavioral invariants
Stack and component-library constraints

commands.description: Inspect a local development page, preview reversible DOM changes and prepare a structured source-code handoff.
whenToUse: Use to inspect a locally running development page and preview reversible DOM-level alternatives.
Use when visual inspection can clarify a later source-code proposal.
notFor: Do not use as a source-code editor or assume previews persist through framework rendering.
Do not inspect production or remote pages without explicit permission.
inputs: Local development URL and current viewport
Target element or specific visual question
Permitted temporary preview scope

commands.description: Perform a focused finishing pass for consistency, spacing, typography and interaction feedback.
whenToUse: Use as a finishing pass after the hierarchy and core behavior are sound.
Use for consistency, spacing, typography and interaction-feedback refinement.
notFor: Do not conceal unresolved information architecture or functional problems.
Do not turn a focused pass into an unrequested redesign.
inputs: Active target and approved direction
Existing constraints, tokens and known findings

commands.description: Remove complexity that does not improve the user task, clarity or system consistency.
whenToUse: Use when the active interface contains unnecessary complexity or competing elements.
Use to simplify a flow while preserving required content and capabilities.
notFor: Do not remove required content just to make the screen minimal.
Do not change the product scope.
inputs: Active target and information hierarchy
Essential user tasks and content that must remain

commands.description: Increase visual distinctiveness without sacrificing clarity, accessibility or product fit.
whenToUse: Use when the direction feels generic and needs more product-specific character.
Use when distinctiveness can increase without reducing clarity or accessibility.
notFor: Do not apply expressive styling when restraint is explicitly requested.
Do not sacrifice task clarity for novelty.
inputs: Active direction and product context
Brand constraints and acceptable expressive range

commands.description: Reduce visual competition while preserving information hierarchy and discoverability.
whenToUse: Use when visual competition distracts from primary content or action.
Use to reduce noise while retaining hierarchy and discoverability.
notFor: Do not hide critical status, warnings, focus or navigation.
Do not remove brand identity without a product reason.
inputs: Active target and current hierarchy
Primary task and essential emphasis

commands.description: Improve semantic color roles and evaluate contrast with explicit confidence limits.
whenToUse: Use to refine semantic color roles, themes and state feedback.
Use when palette application needs adjustment without replacing product identity.
notFor: Do not invent new brand colors when project tokens exist.
Do not claim contrast compliance without actual rendered color-pair evidence.
inputs: Existing color tokens and themes
Actual foreground/background combinations
Brand constraints and state semantics

commands.description: Refine typography roles, scale, line height, measure and readability.
whenToUse: Use to refine typography roles, scale, measure, line height and readability.
Use when text hierarchy or reading comfort is the requested design problem.
notFor: Do not choose fonts before checking available assets and licensing.
Do not use oversized display type as a substitute for hierarchy.
inputs: Current type tokens and available fonts
Real content lengths and language
Target viewports and reading context

commands.description: Improve composition, spacing, alignment, grouping and information density.
whenToUse: Use to change composition, spacing, grouping, alignment or information density.
Use when content is clear but the current arrangement is not serving the task.
notFor: Do not reorder information architecture without understanding the user task.
Do not impose a fixed grid or hero pattern regardless of content.
inputs: Current content order and layout
Viewport, density and interaction requirements
Existing responsive constraints

commands.description: Propose meaningful motion and state feedback while respecting reduced-motion preferences.
whenToUse: Use when motion communicates state, continuity or interaction feedback.
Use when the user requests purposeful animation.
notFor: Do not add decorative loops, scroll hijacking or motion that delays primary actions.
Do not ignore prefers-reduced-motion.
inputs: Target interaction and state transitions
Motion preferences and reduced-motion fallback

commands.description: Review and adapt the experience across viewport sizes, pointer types and input modes.
whenToUse: Use to adapt the experience across viewport sizes, touch, pointer and input modes.
Use when the user requests mobile, tablet or desktop adaptation.
notFor: Do not merely shrink desktop columns without reprioritizing content.
Do not assume one viewport represents all users.
inputs: Target viewport range and device assumptions
Content priorities and supported input modes

commands.description: Strengthen empty, loading, error, overflow, keyboard and edge-case states.
whenToUse: Use to strengthen empty, loading, error, disabled, overflow and keyboard states.
Use when known edge cases or recovery paths need attention.
notFor: Do not invent speculative flows without product evidence.
Do not change core behavior without an approved specification.
inputs: Known states, failure modes and current behavior
Expected recovery and accessibility requirements

commands.description: Find repeated UI patterns that are candidates for reusable components or design tokens.
whenToUse: Use when repeated structures are candidates for shared components, patterns or tokens.
Use when a reusable system should be derived from multiple existing screens.
notFor: Do not abstract one-off elements without stable shared behavior.
Do not create abstractions that obscure the codebase.
inputs: Representative repeated UI examples
Visual and behavioral invariants
Existing module and design-system boundaries
